content_zh:
弱者向命运低头，强者让命运低头。
鲜血从指缝间滴落，在青石板上晕开一朵朵触目惊心的血花。
云澈缓缓站直身体。他的经脉尽断，丹田空空如也。在这苍风大陆，这就是废人中的废人。
但他没有倒下。
因为那颗从天外坠落的珠子，正在他的体内发出第一缕光芒。
"这是什么……"
一股从未感受过的力量，如同洪水般涌入四经八脉。那些断裂的经脉，在这股力量的冲刷下，竟开始以肉眼可见的速度愈合。
不，不仅是愈合。
每一根经脉都比原来宽阔了十倍不止。
云澈抬起头。他知道，从这一刻起，属于他的故事，刚刚开始。
content_en:
Mount Cangshan had been the site of the Blue Wind Empire's founding ceremony five hundred years ago, and now it was the site of the empire's funeral. Yun Che stood on the ancient stone dais where his ancestors had sworn their oaths of fealty, and looked out over the valley below.

Tents. Thousands of them. The rebel army of Feng Zhan, the general who had once been his father's most trusted commander, had camped at the base of Mount Cangshan while they waited for imperial reinforcements that would never come. The empire was already dead. They just hadn't buried it yet.

And in the center of the rebel camp, flying above the largest tent, was the banner of the Profound Handle's Xiao clan.

Yun Che felt something cold settle in his chest. It wasn't surprise. He had known the Profound Handle was backing the rebellion. It was anger — a clean, focused anger that burned away the last traces of the desperate, hopeless prisoner he'd been for three years.

The empire was his birthright. The betrayal was personal. And for the first time since his fall, he let himself think about the future.

Not revenge. Not justice. Not even restoration.

He thought about what kind of world he wanted to build when this was over.

It was a strange thought to have while standing on a mountain overlooking the instruments of his family's destruction. But somehow, the thought steadied him more than any cultivation breakthrough ever could.

He descended the mountain alone, walking through the trees as the sun set behind him, and he began to plan.
